summary.method: Two independent fresh blind reviewers on disjoint six-case blocks

findings: 202: A wins on requested-reference relevance; B retains a prohibited source-hype rebuttal.
206: B wins on factual fidelity; A invents absence of a delivery date.
201, 203, 204 and 205 are genuine task-quality ties; no demonstrated advantage is inferred from equivalence.
claims_audit: All quantities, commands, identifiers, operating conditions and evidence-status claims were checked against the task notes. No additional material unsupported claims were found beyond 206 A.
202 B’s no-load-test/reliability-results statement is supported by the notes but irrelevant to the requested reference subjects. Truth alone does not establish reader relevance.
206 B’s delivery wording is interpreted as limiting a promise, not establishing missing sender knowledge.
block_summaries.exact_checks: Whitespace word counts A/B: 201 107/113; 202 64/92; 203 146/138; 204 123/118; 205 214/216. All requested word limits pass. Required code identifiers and numeric thresholds were checked in the quoted expectation evidence.
eval_feedback: The assertions discriminate useful historical rationale from irrelevant chronology and correctly expose 206 A’s source-omission inference.

202’s fourth assertion permits an accurate reliability rebuttal while its fifth excludes it as irrelevant. These are compatible checks; this distinction should remain explicit in reporting. No criterion was changed.
block_summaries.limitations: Single blind comparison of these six packets only; editorial preferences are provisional, not population-level superiority evidence.

limitations: Single-sample blind editorial judgments for these six assigned cases only; no arm identities inferred and no population-level superiority claimed.
Claims were checked against each supplied task and its two outputs only; no external verification or actor-process claim is available.
Whitespace-delimited word counts verify the requested ranges; they do not establish editorial quality.

eval_feedback.observation: Both copies satisfy all factual/length assertions while repeating scarce source facts. A repeats replaceability through most of the copy; B repeats the warranty.
eval_feedback.suggestion: Keep assertions unchanged for this evaluation. In future tests, assess the positive request to make copy more compelling separately from factual restraint, so compliant word-count padding is not mistaken for effective copy.

eval_feedback.observation: The explicit assertions do not separately name broader representativeness, although the prompt forbids it. Both outputs pass that semantic check: A says “cannot establish preferences ... elsewhere”; B says “cannot establish preference ... other clinics.”
eval_feedback.suggestion: A future assertion could explicitly test that the pilot and optional survey are not generalized to other clinics; current rubric scoring already includes this.
